utterances.text: Well, sir, could you please read the first sentence of Article 1 of the exhibit I just mentioned to you. It's on page 1. Could you please read that aloud. The Red Cross of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. Could you please read it.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... is a state humanitarian, voluntary social organisation of general benefit and interest, which embodies the work of the mission and the principles in the International Committee of the Red Cross and enjoys the special protection -- [In English] Excuse me. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: So the first part of the sentence was: Until a state -- could you please read it back again, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And slowly for the benefit of the Court.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Red Cross of the Croatian Republic of Herceg Bosnia is a state humanitarian, voluntary social organisation of general benefit and interest..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, in the same article but the second paragraph. Would you agree with me that this Red Cross, the Herceg-Bosna Red Cross was established by the law and other regulations of the Herceg-Bosna republic?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The activity of the Red Cross is determined by other regulations because the activity of the Red Cross is about issues of social welfare, health issues, education.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, if we move to Article 4 in page 2 of the same exhibit, Article 4 of the statute of the Herceg-Bosna Red Cross, the last paragraph of that statute.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: The last paragraph of Article 4, sir.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. You confused me. You talked about the statute, but this is probably the law, not the statute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: The law of the Red Cross, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And perhaps the gentleman could be looking at the hard copy because the hard copy is provided to you as opposed to looking at the screen. It might be easier for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: You always have -- under the English version. You have the B/C/S one in the hard copies. But if you have Article --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's in the binder. Help him out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: In Article 4 -- did you find it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: In Article 4, the last paragraph Article 4, it says that "The government of the Herceg-Bosna republic and the relevant ministry shall approve the statute of the Red Cross of the Herceg-Bosna Republic." Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: It was not as you mentioned in the beginning such an independent and neutral organisation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, in part, this was an auxiliary organ helping the federal institutions in the sense of carrying out its mandate and its commitments under the Geneva Conventions. The state, or rather, any state must determine what the purview would be of its Red Cross. As far as I know, in most countries that are members, this is something that is determined by law. In Bosnia-Herzegovina, a law was adopted on the Red Cross at the federal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, you didn't answer my question. Isn't it true that the relevant ministry of the Herceg-Bosna republic monitored the activities of the Herceg-Bosna Red Cross and had the authority to approve the statute?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Just a minute, please. This question contains two questions, two separate matters. I move that my friend keep the matters apart, or the questions. One is the relevant ministry of the Herceg-Bosna, can it monitor the activities of the Herceg-Bosna Red Cross; the other issue being a different issue altogether, did it have the authority to prove the statute? And we've heard evidence about that too: When a social organisation is set up, then the statute is later submitted for approval, and these are two entirely different matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Longone, in your questions, two topics have been addressed. Please take one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that the relevant ministry of the government of the Republic of Herceg-Bosna was entitled -- was in charge to approve the statute of that Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what it says. The government approved the Red Cross statute. The Red Cross statute was drafted by the members of the Red Cross assembly. The reason the statute was approved --

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, we just read Article 4, and it says, The government of the Herceg-Bosna Republic and the relevant ministry shall approve the statute of the Red Cross of the Republic of Herceg-Bosna. Isn't it, is what it says there in the law?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not going to be very helpful -- as the witness articulated earlier, the document says what the document says. If my learned friend is trying to get the witness's evidence about what lays behind the document or how it operates in practice or what laid behind it, that's an entirely different matter, and it was one, in my respectful submission, that the witness was attempting to answer at page 93, line 21. Sorry, line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the Prosecutor through these documents and his questions would like to establish a connection between the fact that the Red Cross of Herceg-Bosna was dependent upon the government. You answered briefly by saying that in democratic states, if I remember correctly, the law provides for the creation and monitoring of Red Cross organisation. I must say that I don't know much about this. As far as you know, in various countries - let's take the case of Spain, for instance - do you know whether it is a government that prepares a text on the Red Cross, and the statute needs to be approved by the government? Is this how it works?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know specifically about Spain, but I can tell you about the background and the reasons why the statute needed approving by the relevant federal body and the relevant ministry because the government works like this: A particular ministry - in this case, ministry of social welfare - puts forward a proposal, and that is why the ministry is relevant here, the reason being this: In the law on the Red Cross in the Red Cross statute, there are activities that are listed. There is work that is specified that is directly linked to the mandate of the Red Cross. If there is no correlation, if there is no document that has been adopted, it is as a result difficult to protect and preserve one's mandate. And then let's go back to the original story. It's very difficult to persuade someone to let through an employee of the Red Cross carrying a Red Cross card. It is highly important for everyone, including the appropriate authorities, to be familiar with the function and nature of the work of the Red Cross. The country itself was duty-bound under a set of international conventions that it would monitor and support such activities, so this is the gist, and that is why laws are passed. That is why approval is granted for the statute in order not to have any contradictions there. In its later work, the Red Cross would be implementing everything, all of its commitments under the statute. The law provides general principles and modalities in the broadest possible sense as to how the organisation would work and what its links would be to the authorities, in essence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Longone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir, this was a Red Cross that was supposed to work for all the people, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those facing certain situations. All those in needs but always in keeping with its own needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And this organisation, sir, was the one that -- the only reason why they was not working with the Bosnia-Herzegovina Red Cross was because there were broken communication links and because of the war situation?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If we go back to the Red Cross statute, the regional Red Cross of Herceg-Bosna, this invokes in its preamble the statute of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Red Cross, which allows for the possibility for the Red Crosses throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina to be established in municipalities, in regions, too, if that is what the circumstances call for, the statute from before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. On Article 20 of the same document we were discussing, the same decree in page 6.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Article 20.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: It refers again that the government of Herceg-Bosna of the Republic of Herceg-Bosna and the relevant ministry shall monitor application of the law in the activities and work of the Red Cross of the Republic of Herceg-Bosna, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, and I find it logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And did you find logical also Article 21: The Red Cross of the Republic of Herceg-Bosna shall take over all rights, obligations, and property of the Red Cross of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the territory of the Croatian republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: This is the Red Cross, the Herceg-Bosna Red Cross that you mentioned that was working for all people during the war?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because part of the Herceg-Bosna Red Cross was the municipal Red Cross in Mostar. All the property that the Red Cross had, the municipal organisation in Mostar, now became the property of all the organisations that were active within the Herceg-Bosna Red Cross, not just Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: And sir, isn't it true that the reality was that the Herceg-Bosna Red Cross didn't want to work with the Bosnia and Herzegovina Red Cross and didn't want to work with the Bosnian Muslim people, isn't it? You were part of it. You know that very well, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where you got this conclusion. Personally, I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have two exhibits to finish, and they're very important, and then we finish with this part of the cross-examination. If you allow me, two more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is already 7.00. If it's only a few minutes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: If you see Exhibit P10691.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: 10691. P10691. It's in the binder. That one.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not in this binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. LONGONE
utterances.text: It's in the second binder, sir.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO SIMUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] One minute. [Interpretation] Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm told that this is not in e-court, and if it is not, I would object to this document being shown to the witness at this point in time. We certainly should be entitled to look at the document and to raise any objections that may be necessary, and it seems to me that even going through two documents assuming that they are in e-court is going to take about ten minutes at this rate. So I would ask, given that the translators have been working very hard, that we end the day. We can begin again tomorrow. We've got plenty of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Longone, you have heard the objections. We need to check whether this has been downloaded into the e-court system. Since we are in no hurry, we can resume tomorrow. It is now a few minutes past 7.00. I would like to apologise vis-a-vis the interpreters because we have overstepped our time. We shall look into this again at a quarter past 2.00 and address this document tomorrow, P1069. Enjoy your evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 22nd day of October, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
